title: Upstage API Pricing: All Models and Costs (2026)
summary: Upstage API pricing depends on which model you choose. Review the rates for each product to determine your costs before committing.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits in Upstage billing


Only if your bill is made of the line items you priced does the $400 survive.


The extras that break that assumption are output tokens, long inputs, retried parses, how the vendor counts pages, and quotes that never appear on a price page.


### Output tokens and long documents


On Solar language models, the meter is tokens, and **output tokens cost more than input tokens** . A workload that summarizes a long document is cheap to read and cheap to answer.


If a workload rewrites or expands text, it pays the higher rate on most of its volume, so estimate output length separately instead of applying one blended rate.


Attach long context and the opposite problem appears: each call bills every extra page of context you attach again. A chat that resends a whole contract per question multiplies the input meter by the number of questions.


### Retries, page counting and rejected files in billing


When a parse fails and your code retries it, that is a second run on the same pages. Document Parse and Information Extract meter pages, not tokens, so if retries are automatic, your real page count is the document count times the attempts.


Count pages the way the vendor does, not the way your file viewer does. A scanned bundle, a file with blank separator sheets, or a PDF with long appendices bills by what the parser processes.


Sample a few real files and compare the billed count against your own before you extrapolate.


If you wrap those calls in an intake flow on[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , from email attachment through Document Parse and Extract to a spreadsheet, the meter on the workflow side is the run, not the steps inside it: 1 credit per run, whether you built it as a two-step workaround or split it into ten smaller, safer steps.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so on their pricing pages the same discipline raises the cost of the flow. Upstage still bills each page at the per-1,000-page rates above, so the table remains what you budget from.


### Batch and caching discounts: what exists and what does not


On other vendors' platforms, cached input and batch processing are the two levers that cut a token bill most. Treat them as unconfirmed for Upstage until the pricing page for the exact product you call lists them.


For Document Parse and Information Extract in particular, don't assume a token-style cache applies to a page-metered call.


### Upstage enterprise and private deployment pricing


You won't find a unit price to put in a spreadsheet for private or on-premises deployment, because Upstage quotes it instead of listing it.


Ask for it in the same units you used above, pages for parsing and tokens for language models, so you can compare it with the public bill directly.
